Build the feature-planner terminal SKILL. Create src/pathly_data/core/skills/planning/feature-decompose.md — the terminal emitter that posts 2-5 sibling GOAL cards (type=goal) to the feature board. Read pathly/features/planner-hierarchy/SPEC.md (G1). The skill: (1) reads the feature's starting spec + existing goals on the board + any feature-level artifacts (ARCHITECTURE/RESEARCH/DESIGN at the feature root); (2) proposes 2-5 goals (e.g. backend-api / frontend / db) each with a scope + acceptance boundary; (3) posts each as type=goal via POST /comms/post {board=feature, scope=<feature>, from=planner, type=goal}; (4) wires depends_on between goals where real (frontend depends on backend contract); (5) stamps each goal's context_refs at the feature artifacts that exist (produce-once/inherit-many — absent in the light tier, present after the consultation tier). This ONE skill is the terminal for EVERY rigor tier (light = run standalone; consultation = run as the feature-consultation flow's terminal). MIRROR planning/dag-sketch mechanics but emit type=goal, NOT type=task. Register in src/pathly_data/core/skills/composition.yaml (no_defaults; fragments: comms-post + completion-report). Done when: the skill file exists and composes.

(b) Add a goal-counting exit gate: count(type=goal, scope=feature) >= 2 -> DONE, else NO_GOALS_SEEDED. Implement count_goals_for_feature in db/queries/comms_messages.py (mirror count_tasks_for_goal in comms_tasks.py) and an on_feature_goal_count rule branch in fsm/engine_transitions.py evaluate_transition_rules (mirror the on_board_count Level 2.6 block, but scope-keyed not goal-keyed). Rework src/pathly_data/core/skills/planning/prd-import.md to emit the board-native goal-DAG hierarchy instead of the old conversation model. The updated skill: (1) detects BMAD epics/stories vs generic PRDs; (2) parses args as <path/to/PRD.md> [project_scope_or_root], not legacy <feature-name> <PRD_PATH>; (3) maps PRD title/project scope -> project, BMAD epics -> project-board type=feature cards via POST /comms/post, and BMAD stories -> feature-board type=goal cards; (4) scaffolds pathly/features/<slug>/SPEC.md for each emitted feature and materializes that feature board/root goal, reusing planning/project-decompose mechanics; (5) preserves depends_on at every hierarchy level: PRD/BMAD epic dependencies become feature-card depends_on, story dependencies become goal-card depends_on, and later goal decomposition keeps task dependencies inside the task DAG; (6) always stores returned board message_id values in depends_on, never slugs/titles; (7) uses idempotency/skip-if-down mechanics from the canonical task-DAG posting pattern, adapted to feature/goal children; (8) removes legacy CONVERSATION_PROMPTS.md, phase split, and 4/8-file PRD plan output entirely. Register in src/pathly_data/core/skills/composition.yaml with no_defaults and fragments: code-query, comms-post, completion-report. artifacts.summary:
- **The recursion model** — one decompose pattern applied at three levels (project→features, feature→goals, goal→tasks), where only the emitted item type changes and siblings stay board-aware.
- **Current state** — a table of what exists (goal→tasks) versus what is new (feature→goals, project→features) and what is partial (PRD/BMAD import).
- **G1 feature-planner** — the immediate deliverable: split a feature spec into 2–5 sibling goal cards, with a light/full/consultation rigor ladder and a human checkpoint.
- **G2 project-planner** — top-of-funnel planner that splits one big spec on the project board into N feature cards, each with its own starting spec.
- **G0 reliability foundation & G3 import modernization** — the prerequisite loud-failure/telemetry hardening at the bottom level, and reworking PRD/BMAD import to feed the new goal-DAG model.
- **Design constraints & sequencing** — locked rules (nested readable storage, board as awareness substrate, reuse over reinvention) and the bottom-up build order G0→G1→G2→G3, plus non-goals.
